title: security-questionnaire-response-matrix-and-indemnity-cost-simulator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Manual redline handling for MSA/DPA and Security Questionnaires (SQs) is a major bottleneck for sales and renewals. Small indemnity/liability redlines often cause multi-day legal reviews and ad-hoc pricing concessions. Goal: Build a deterministic triage + response matrix for SQ + contract redlines and a pricing simulator that estimates indemnity/liability exposure and recommended price/terms delta to empower commercial and legal to make faster decisions. The feature should reduce contract turnaround time, surface consistent guidance, and enable partial automation for low-risk requests.
acceptance_criteria: Risk scoring engine implemented that classifies redlines into Low/Medium/High with explanation strings
SQ response matrix mapped to common controls (e.g., SOC, encryption, data residency) with templated answers and required approvals
Indemnity Cost Simulator returns recommended price delta and suggested indemnity cap tiers given customer revenue band and contract term
UI exposes redline risk score and pricing recommendation in contract intake and Redwood Console contract dashboard
Auto-approve rule implemented for < 3 minor redlines and low risk score with audit log entries
Legal and Sales sign-off obtained on final thresholds and templates (documented in Confluence link)
notes: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after sales ops retrospective; attached initial spreadsheet of redline categories (Confluence: /enterprise/contracts/redline-catalog).

2026-02-27: Scoping sync with Legal (Sonia Martinez) and Sales (Marco Ruiz). Legal requested explicit three-tier indemnity framework: Limited (cap = 1x ARR), Standard (cap = 5x ARR), Full (no cap) — also requested additional guardrails for escrow/third-party claims.

2026-03-03: Engineering feasibility review: ENG backend can add clause classification microservice (ENG-5233). Work estimate ~3 sprints if we include ML-assisted clause extraction; MVP can use rule-based heuristics to start.

2026-03-05: Prototype indemnity simulator spreadsheet created by PM; includes inputs: customer ARR band, contract term, exposure multiplier, and suggested uplift percentage. Shared with Pricing. Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/indemnity-simulator-proto

2026-03-07: Decision: Launch MVP with rule-based scoring and templates for top 20 redline patterns. Defer ML clause extraction to phase 2. Trade-off: faster time-to-value vs lower recall on unusual clauses.
2026-03-09: Legal feedback (Sonia): require audit trail and ability to override auto-recommendations. Also requested daily summary digest for legal ops of auto-approved items.
2026-03-10: PM update: Wireframes for contract intake UI updated (Design spike DES-1122 referenced). Created acceptance test plan; next steps: ENG task creation and Legal template finalization.

Follow-ups: 1) Create ENG tickets for scoring engine and API integration (ENG-7002, ENG-7003). 2) Add templates to Confluence and implement QA script for randomized SQs. 3) Schedule legal playbook review on 2026-03-18.
review_feedback: Legal (Sonia Martinez): Add explicit fallback flow when customer refuses standard indemnity cap; require legal review and pricing desk escalation.
Sales Ops (Marco Ruiz): Include suggested negotiation language and a one-line rationale to help AEs justify price uplifts to customers.
Pricing (Leah O'Connor): Simulator should output both percent uplift and absolute dollar estimate; incorporate discounting rules tied to committed term lengths.
implementation_notes: MVP approach: rule-based clause matcher + deterministic scoring mapping to templates. Store templates in Confluence and surface via API.
Longer-term: train a clause-extraction model to identify indemnity/loss allocation language and detect synonyms for common redlines.
Observability: add contract-turn KPI to Console (avg days to signature) and telemetry for auto-approve rate and manual overrides.
Security: all contract artifacts stored in KMS-backed bucket; ensure audit logs preserved for 7 years per retention policy.
